html:
A long study of Indian religion, science and customs written by the Khwarazmian scholar al-Biruni and finished in about 1030. Its Arabic title means roughly "a verification of what India says".

Al-Biruni came from Khwarazm on the Amu Darya. In 1017 Mahmud of Ghazni conquered his homeland and took him to Ghazni. He then went with Mahmud's court on campaigns into the Punjab. While Mahmud's armies were looting temples, al-Biruni learned Sanskrit, talked with Brahmin scholars and read their books.

The result covers Hindu philosophy and gods, caste, festivals, law, geography, calendars and above all Indian astronomy and mathematics. He tried to describe Indian ideas in their own terms and compared them with Greek thought, rather than simply condemning them. That care has led some to call him the first anthropologist. The book remained the best outside account of India for centuries.
sum: A long study of Indian religion, science and customs written by the Khwarazmian scholar al-Biruni and finished in about 1030. Its Arabic title means roughly "a verification of what India says".
